title: Problem memory gets its own switch and a day-2 check of whether the Lead re-asks stored facts
request: Give the Lead's problem memory note a switch of its own (DCLAB_LEAD_PROBLEM_MEMORY), move its words into a prompt file, and measure live, small and capped, whether memory alone stops the Lead from asking a person again for facts they stated on day 1.
spec: Note present only with a switch on, framed as data, read from dclab_rnd/prompts/lead_problem_memory.md; eight invented dev stories, the Lead's first day-2 turn with memory off and on, qwen/qwen3.8-flash, scored by code (re-asked facts, questions, named facts), at most EUR 0.30.
plan: add the memory switch beside the bounded loop's in lead_choice.json and the environment
move the note's words into a prompt file and rerun the prompt and harness gates
write tests for the switch, the framing and the prompt file
write eight dev stories with facts and keywords, and the scoring by code
dry run with a scripted client, then one live run under the cap
read every question by hand and write the result for a non-expert

decisions.decision: The memory switch lives in decision_loop.settings beside the loop's switch
decisions.why: set_settings rewrites lead_choice.json from settings(); a key kept elsewhere would be dropped every time the loop's switch is written

decisions.decision: The note's words were moved unchanged, with no new instruction to avoid re-asking
decisions.why: the check measures memory as it is; adding an instruction would measure a new prompt instead

decisions.decision: Day 1 writes the facts the way Home's hand-off does, without a live day-1 conversation
decisions.why: the same Problem Base lines and field names as draft/memory.py hand_off, with no spend and no noise from a day-1 model

decisions.decision: The code score is reported as fixed, and a hand reading is reported beside it
decisions.why: the rule was fixed before the run; changing it after seeing the replies would tune the scorer to the answer

change: decision_loop: MEMORY_ENV, problem_memory in settings/set_settings, problem_memory_enabled. case_agent: memory_note() from the prompt file lead_problem_memory, sent when the loop or the memory switch is on. agent_eval/memory_day2.py with its stories file; tests/test_lead_problem_memory.py; AEV-129 and HRN-139 rerun for the new prompt's hash.

findings.defect: The code rule counts a question that only mentions a stored fact as a re-ask of it.
findings.scenario: MD2-02 with memory on asked 'when the model says a customer will cancel within 90 days, what actually happens?'; the rule counted the horizon as asked again, though the question built on it.
findings.cause: the re-ask test is any question sentence holding a fact's keywords; the value words (90 days, Sunday night) appear when the Lead uses the fact
findings.fix: not fixed in this run; next: a re-ask must ask for the fact (an interrogative about it, or alternatives offered for it), checked on these replies before a new run
findings.test: agent_runs/live_tests/20261119T165904Z-memory-day2 replies, read by hand: 5 of the 6 code matches are of this kind

findings.defect: The code rule misses a re-ask of the outcome written in plain words.
findings.scenario: MD2-03 with memory off asked 'should the number it predicts be bikes rented, bikes returned, or the net imbalance?'; the keyword bikes_rented did not match the plain words.
findings.cause: story keywords hold the column name only, not its words without underscores
findings.fix: not fixed in this run; next: match a column name with spaces as well as underscores

findings.defect: Without memory the Lead asks again for facts the person already gave.
findings.scenario: Memory off, read by hand: MD2-03 and MD2-06 asked which column to predict, MD2-04 asked whether it scores new applications or loans on the book; with memory on none did clearly.
findings.cause: the stored facts are not in the request when memory is off; the case file starts empty on day 2
findings.fix: the switch exists, off by default; turning it on is the owner's decision after a fixed scorer and a fresh run

measurements.name: Memory day 2: the Lead's first day-2 turn, memory off against on, 8 invented dev stories
measurements.gate: none: a paired count to read; fewer re-asked facts with memory on would mean memory helps
measurements.result: code: re-asked 2 (off) and 4 (on) of 24 facts, 0 better, 2 worse, 6 equal; by hand: 3 (off) and 0 (on, 1 borderline); questions 12 and 9; 84 of 84 calls kept with thinking
measurements.next: fix the re-ask rule (ask for, not mention; column words), check it on these replies, then run fresh dev stories with two repeats
limits: hand reading by the builder after the run, no blind second reader
the code rule is known to be wrong in both directions

outcome: Memory now has its own switch, off by default, with its words in a prompt file under the prompt gate. Live, the code score said memory made re-asking worse (2 against 4), but a hand reading shows the rule counted questions that used the stored facts; read by hand memory removed the clear re-asks (3 against 0). The check needs a better rule before its number can be trusted.
lessons: A keyword re-ask rule penalises the arm that uses the facts: it must test asking for a fact, not mentioning it
Read the replies before believing a code score, even a score fixed before the run
Most day-2 questions were about the decision and who reads the output, which no one had stored
risks: The code score alone would have led to the wrong conclusion that memory hurts
The hand count is small and unblinded
